architectureInvariants.rule: ScaleOps remains the parent SaaS application; ProofArena remains a module inside the existing client and server.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: A second app would duplicate auth, routing, deployment, and persistence boundaries.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 2 boundary ADR plus migration plan

architectureInvariants.rule: ProofArena composes existing challenge, offer, execution-plan, proof, matching, provider, and opportunity domains instead of copying them.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Parallel implementations would create incompatible contracts and data ownership.

architectureInvariants.rule: Code outside the frontend ProofArena module uses its public entry point; feature domains must not depend on product composition.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Private imports would make migration order and ownership unstable.

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/main.jsx remains the browser entry and mounts the query client and router.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Provider ordering or router initialization can fail globally.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Framework/bootstrap change with app smoke tests

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/App.jsx owns top-level provider composition.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Auth and route hydration can render in the wrong order.

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx remains the frontend route registration authority.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Duplicate routers or route drift can create inaccessible pages and guard bypasses.

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/constants/routes.js remains the route-path constant source used by features and navigation.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Scattered path strings would break aliases, breadcrumbs, and role fallbacks.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 4 route governance with import migration

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/config/routeMetadata.js remains metadata, not a second router; its 34 known coverage gaps must not be treated as absent routes.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Consumers can incorrectly hide or reject active routes.

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/layouts/PublicLayout.jsx owns the active public shell; RootLayout.jsx remains a compatibility concern until proven removable.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Public header/footer nesting and auth pages can regress.

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/layouts/DashboardLayout.jsx owns the provider/shared dashboard shell.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Sidebar sizing, auth loading, and provider content can break.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 36 provider dashboard work after shell tests

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/layouts/ClientLayout.jsx and AdminLayout.jsx retain distinct role-specific shells.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Client/admin navigation or access boundaries can leak across roles.

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/layouts/useSidebarShell.js and client/src/hooks/useSidebarState.js coordinate dashboard shell state; mobile state is not a second persistent desktop state.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Empty layout gaps, stale drawers, or localStorage regressions can occur.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Dashboard shell refactor after responsive tests

architectureInvariants.rule: SidebarCore.jsx remains the shared sidebar renderer used by provider, client, and admin wrappers.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Manual sidebar copies would diverge in active-state, filtering, and accessibility behavior.

architectureInvariants.rule: Public, provider, client, and admin navigation remain configuration-driven from client/src/config/navigation/.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Hardcoded navigation would bypass route/access helpers.

architectureInvariants.rule: AuthProvider.jsx, useAuthStore.js, and the route-guard suite remain the current frontend auth/session boundary.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Protected content can flash, redirect loops can form, or roles can leak.

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/services/apiClient.js remains the shared HTTP transport boundary; components should not create another Axios/fetch client.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Token refresh, credentials, error translation, and base URL behavior would diverge.

architectureInvariants.rule: Button.jsx, PageHeader.jsx, and AppStateShell.jsx are shared UI foundations; compatibility wrappers must be audited before removal.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Visual, semantic, and accessibility behavior would fragment.

architectureInvariants.rule: accessPolicy.js, navigationFilter.js, navigationActive.js, and routeValidation.js remain centralized policy/helpers rather than duplicated component logic.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Role checks, active states, and route safety would become inconsistent.

architectureInvariants.rule: server/src/server.js remains the process entry for database, HTTP, sockets, and workers.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Startup order and process lifecycle can fail.

architectureInvariants.rule: server/src/app.js remains the Express composition root for global middleware, webhooks, routes, and errors.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Middleware ordering, webhook parsing, and error responses can break.

architectureInvariants.rule: Both server/src/routes/index.js and server/src/routes/v1/index.js are active; their 233 dual-mounted operations cannot be removed casually.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Existing clients can receive 404s or different middleware behavior.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 1.3 API-version ADR and migration telemetry

architectureInvariants.rule: The normal backend dependency direction remains route to controller to service to model; known inline and partial flows are exceptions documented in the traceability matrix.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Business logic can become untestable or bypass validation/security.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 3 module migration one vertical slice at a time

architectureInvariants.rule: server/src/modules/auth/ is an active auth implementation, but legacy auth controller/service generations remain compatibility risks, not deletion candidates.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Removing the wrong generation can break login, refresh, or verification flows.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 23 after caller and endpoint contract tests

architectureInvariants.rule: Both auth and role middleware naming generations remain active until route-by-route migration proves otherwise.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Authorization can weaken or legitimate requests can be rejected.

architectureInvariants.rule: apiResponse.js, AppError.js, asyncHandler.js, and global error middleware define response/error behavior.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Frontend contracts can receive inconsistent status and payload shapes.

architectureInvariants.rule: server/src/config/db.js owns database connection initialization and model registration side effects.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Startup, indexes, or registered models can change unexpectedly.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Database migration with rollback and model tests

architectureInvariants.rule: loadEnv.js and env.js own server environment loading/validation; secrets remain outside documentation and source.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Deployments can start with missing or unsafe configuration.

architectureInvariants.rule: Request validation remains route-bound through existing validators and validation middleware; duplicate validators must be mapped before consolidation.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Invalid or unauthorized payloads can reach business logic.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 5 contract layer after endpoint tests

architectureInvariants.rule: server/src/models/User.js is security-critical identity persistence used by auth, admin, and user services.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Schema changes can invalidate credentials, roles, sessions, and user ownership.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 23 with migration and rollback plan

architectureInvariants.rule: UserProfile.js and ProviderProfile.js are active profile persistence; model aliases and the unresolved VerifiedOutcome reference must be preserved until ownership is decided.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Profile reads/population can fail or data can split across collections.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Profile stage after model/ref audit and tests

architectureInvariants.rule: MarketplaceTransaction.js, Invoice.js, and Subscription.js are financial records and must not change without contract, migration, and webhook tests.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Money, invoices, subscriptions, and reconciliation can be corrupted.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Payments stage with Stripe regression suite

architectureInvariants.rule: Challenge.model.js and OutcomeChallenge.model.js are overlapping concepts; neither is canonical by audit evidence alone.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Premature merging can orphan data or break service queries.

architectureInvariants.rule: OutcomeOffer.model.js, ExecutionPlan.model.js, ProofAsset.model.js, and MatchRecord.model.js form connected ProofArena workflows.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Cross-domain lifecycle and ownership references can break.

architectureInvariants.rule: Settings.js and UserSettings.js overlap; collection ownership and read/write callers must be established before consolidation.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Settings can diverge or be silently lost.

architectureInvariants.rule: scripts/check-module-boundaries.mjs is the executable boundary policy for client/server module dependency direction.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Shared foundations can start importing product modules and create cycles.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Stage 3 boundary ADR with script updates

architectureInvariants.rule: client/src/styles/tokens.css remains the shared design-token source.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Hardcoded values and incompatible themes can spread across layouts.

architectureInvariants.rule: Shared config, constants, errors, stores, and utilities must not depend on feature/page/route implementations.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Dependency inversion and circular ownership can result.

architectureInvariants.rule: Frontend and backend source remain physically and import-wise separated; no source-level cross-boundary import was found.
architectureInvariants.riskIfViolated: Browser/server bundling and secret boundaries would be compromised.
architectureInvariants.futureStageAllowedToChange: Only through an explicit shared-contract package ADR

forbiddenActions.action: Create a separate ProofArena app, repository, router, or deployment.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: It duplicates the verified ScaleOps platform boundary.
forbiddenActions.saferAlternative: Extend the existing ProofArena module boundary
forbiddenActions.allowedOnlyAfter: Stage 2 ADR explicitly changes product boundary

forbiddenActions.action: Create another route-constant registry.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: routes.js already owns centralized paths.
forbiddenActions.allowedOnlyAfter: Stage 4 route migration with all importers updated

forbiddenActions.action: Create another frontend router or hidden nested route stack.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: AppRoutes.jsx owns route and guard composition.

forbiddenActions.action: Create another public/provider/client/admin layout for the same surface.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Current shells and compatibility layouts already overlap.
forbiddenActions.allowedOnlyAfter: Stage 1.2 ownership decision and browser tests

forbiddenActions.action: Create another sidebar engine or manually duplicate nav rendering.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: SidebarCore already handles rendering, active state, filtering, and accessibility.

forbiddenActions.action: Create another auth provider, user store, or route-guard family.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Current auth state and compatibility layers are already complex.

forbiddenActions.action: Bypass route guards or render protected content before auth resolves.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: It creates security UX leaks and redirect instability.

forbiddenActions.action: Hardcode role or permission logic in arbitrary UI components.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Central access policy and backend middleware already exist.
forbiddenActions.saferAlternative: Extend centralized policy and backend enforcement

forbiddenActions.action: Create another Axios/fetch client or make raw component requests.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: apiClient.js owns credentials, refresh, and errors.
forbiddenActions.saferAlternative: Add/reuse a feature service using apiClient

forbiddenActions.action: Add a third backend API registry or silently change mount prefixes.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Two active registries already expose 233 dual mounts.

forbiddenActions.action: Put substantial business logic in route files.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: The verified normal flow is route-controller-service-model.

forbiddenActions.action: Add another auth, role, validation, error, rate-limit, or sanitization middleware generation.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Parallel generations already create governance risk.

forbiddenActions.action: Edit or merge models without reading the model usage map.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Aliases, overlaps, references, and sensitive fields are active.

forbiddenActions.action: Delete files because they appear unused.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Dynamic imports, aliases, compatibility exports, or runtime registration may not be obvious.

forbiddenActions.action: Merge overlapping Challenge, Settings, User, Profile, or middleware files immediately.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Canonical ownership is not established.

forbiddenActions.action: Modify package, lock, environment, build, or deployment files casually.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: These files control runtime and deployment topology.

forbiddenActions.action: Copy secrets or real environment values into code or documentation.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: It exposes credentials and violates audit boundaries.
forbiddenActions.saferAlternative: Refer only to variable names and secret-management docs

forbiddenActions.action: Add dependencies without explicit stage approval.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: It changes build/runtime risk outside the audited architecture.
forbiddenActions.saferAlternative: Use existing dependencies or document the need
forbiddenActions.allowedOnlyAfter: Approved implementation stage and dependency review

forbiddenActions.action: Convert placeholders or preview data into fake production behavior.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Business-looking fallbacks can hide API failures and mislead users.
forbiddenActions.saferAlternative: Keep clearly labeled placeholder or use honest empty/error state
forbiddenActions.allowedOnlyAfter: Owning feature stage with real contract/data

forbiddenActions.action: Move code across module/shared boundaries without checking imports.
forbiddenActions.whyForbidden: Shared-to-feature dependencies and cycles can result.
forbiddenActions.saferAlternative: Move one tested vertical slice with public exports
forbiddenActions.allowedOnlyAfter: Stage 3 boundary plan and passing boundary checker
